title: Celine Dion Slips and Falls Onstage in Paris
text:
Celine Dion quickly recovered after slipping and falling onstage Wednesday during her comeback residency in France, reassuring the audience before continuing her performance.
videocirculating on social media, the 58-year-old Canadian singer apparently caught her pants on a heel while performing “Dans un autre monde.” Dion rose, signaled with a thumbs-up and resumed singing. She did not appear seriously hurt.
The fall came during Dion’s sold-out, five-week series of concerts at Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, a suburb of Paris. The run, which began last month, marked her first full concert performances since 2020.
announcedin 2022 that she had stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological condition that has disrupted her movement and ability to sing.
Dion canceled eight European concerts after disclosing the diagnosis. She said uncontrollable muscle spasms affected daily activities, including walking, and sometimes kept her vocal cords from working as they had before.
“I’m working hard with my sports medicine therapist every day to build back my strength and my ability to perform again but I have to admit it’s been a struggle,” Dion said at the time.
According to RareDiseases.org, stiff-person syndrome can cause rigidity and spasms in the torso and limbs. Noise, touch, and emotional distress may trigger symptoms, and there is no direct cure, though medications and other therapies can help manage them.
Dion’s comeback followed years of postponed and canceled performances as she worked to regain the strength and vocal control required to sing live.
saidshe had taken potentially fatal amounts of Valium while trying to control stiffness and spasms before doctors helped her stop. She also described suffering broken ribs and episodes in which her hands and feet became immobile.
Dion told NBC’s “Today” show at the time that she had concealed her illness while caring for her children and her late husband, Rene Angelil, who had cancer. She also pledged that she would perform again, saying, “I’m going to go back onstage, even if I have to crawl.”
Dion chronicled her illness in the Amazon Prime Video documentary “I Am Celine Dion,” which premiered in June 2024.
announced10 Paris concerts scheduled across September and October. She said the performances would be the greatest birthday gift of her life.
Dion, a five-time Grammy winner from Quebec, achieved worldwide fame with “My Heart Will Go On” from the 1997 film “Titanic.”
